sections.history: Tirupputtur lies in Sivagangai district on the road between Madurai and Karaikudi, and its Shiva temple is counted as the sixth of the Tevaram shrines of the Pandya country, which makes it a Paadal Petra Sthalam. The saints of the Tevaram sang the Lord here as Tiruthalinathar, and the town keeps the old name Tiruputhur, the sacred town of the anthill. Inscriptions in the temple record a long line of patronage: the structure is chiefly of the Chola age, with later maintenance and additions by Pandya and Chera patrons, and gifts of lamps and endowments for perpetual worship are cut into the stone. The village appears in these records as a Brahmadeya settlement within the Koluvur kurram of its day. The founding of the shrine itself is not firmly dated, so it is best held as ancient rather than fixed to a single reign.
sections.architecture: The temple opens through an east-facing gopuram into a complex of three enclosing prakarams. The Lord is a swayambhu linga, said to have appeared of his own accord, and the mandapam before the sanctum is carried on finely sculpted pillars. The goddess Sivakami, also known as Soundarya Nayaki, has her shrine to the north of the main sanctum. In the outer third prakaram stands a separate shrine of Tirunageswarar, and a west-facing shrine of Yoga Bhairavar, whose festival is a high point of the temple year, completes the circuit. The sacred waters of the temple are named in the sources as the Thali and Sivagangai teerthams.
sections.legends: Tradition gives the place two stories. The sage Valmiki is said to have performed penance here in a forest of kondrai trees until an anthill, a puthu in Tamil, rose around him; pleased, Shiva appeared beside it and blessed him, and the name Tiruputhur recalls that moment. In the other account the goddess Mahalakshmi longed to behold the Lord's cosmic dance, and Shiva granted her the sight in the Gauri Thandavam, sometimes called the Lakshmi Thandavam. In gratitude she worshipped him here, and from this the name Tiruthalinathar is traditionally explained. Both stories speak of a Lord who reveals himself where devotion waits, and they are told here as tradition rather than recorded history.
sections.festivals: Two festivals mark the temple year. The Chithirai Bhairavar festival is held in April or May in honour of Yoga Bhairavar, and Karthikai Champaka Sashti is observed in November or December. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are kept as at every Shiva temple. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Come to Tirupputtur without haste, for it is a quiet town and the temple keeps its own unhurried pace. Enter beneath the eastern gopuram and pass through the pillared mandapam to the swayambhu Tiruthalinathar, the Lord who is said to have appeared of his own accord. Turn then to the goddess Sivakami in her shrine and walk the three prakarams slowly, pausing at the shrines of Tirunageswarar and Yoga Bhairavar. Let the thought of Valmiki's long penance and Lakshmi's vision of the dance settle in you. Many pilgrims take the temple as one stop on a journey through the Shaiva shrines of the Pandya country.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; published hours differ between sources, so confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Tirupputtur lies on the road between Madurai and Karaikudi, about 22 km from Karaikudi, 27 km from Sivagangai and roughly 60 km from Madurai, which has the nearest major airport. Karaikudi is the nearest sizeable railway town, and buses serve Tirupputtur from the surrounding towns. Confirm local routes and timetables before travelling.
